name: Energy conversion
seoTitle: Energy conversion Calculator — Formula, Units & Example
seoDesc: Energy conversion: answer 9 values and the page computes the result when you press Calculate — formula and worked example included.
summary: The Energy conversion calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports joule immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. It is built for a recipe, a shopping list, a travel plan or a form that asks for a unit you do not use. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the Energy conversion calculator work?
sections.html:
The Energy conversion calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports joule in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the figures it asks for.

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html: • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilowatt hours. The unit chip switches it to any of the 33 supported units.

sections.title: The formula behind the Energy conversion calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Joule=3600 × watt-hour
Calorie=(125 ÷ 523) × joule
Joule=105506000 × therm
Joule=4184000000 × ton of TNT
Joule=(34516213 ÷ 2500000000000000000000000000000) × temperature
Joule=(80108831 ÷ 500000000000000000000000000) × electronovolt

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Energy, opening in joules
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilowatt hours
  • Energy, opening in electronvolts
  • Temperature, opening in kelvins
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Mass, opening in electron rest masses

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Energy conversion calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Converting a figure someone quoted you so you can compare it
  • Checking a product listing against the measurements you work with
  • Filling in a form that asks for imperial or metric values

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

sections.title: What are the limits worth knowing?
sections.html:
Every tool draws a boundary somewhere. For the Energy conversion calculator, these are the ones that matter:

  • The unit chips cover the units listed on the page. A historical or regional unit that is missing can still be used by converting it to a listed unit first.
  • The calculator reports what the relationship implies; it does not judge whether the inputs themselves are sensible, so a figure that is out by a factor of ten will produce an answer that is out by the same factor.

faq.q: What does the Energy conversion calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns joule. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Energy conversion calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 1 field in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter joule in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Joule opens in joules and the chip beside it offers 33 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Energy conversion calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
